newsitem.title: POLAND: IMF LAUDS POLAND FLOOD RELIEF, ZLOTY DROP TOO DEEP.
newsitem.headline: IMF LAUDS POLAND FLOOD RELIEF, ZLOTY DROP TOO DEEP.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IFM) praised on Tuesday the Polish government for trying to take the middle-ground between efforts to increase the scope of its flood relief and the need to maintain financial stability.

"The government is trying to be responsive but it is also trying to remain responsible marcro-economically and that is how I read the package of decisions made today," IMF representative to Poland Markus Rodlauer told Reuters.

"I also support the government's efforts to keep the overall macro balances intact and to protect as much as possible the state finances in particular the budget deficit which should not be allowed to increase," he added.
Rodlauer said Poland's overall relative economic health did not justify Tuesday's sharp fall of the zloty.
"I see the basic marcro fundementals to continue to be relatively sound in that context I feel that today's drop in the zloty was obviously excessive," he added.
The zloty fell five percent against the currency basket to its lowest level ever at 5.69 percent below the parity rate without triggering an expected central bank intervention to prop up the zloty.

The government wants to amend this year's budget to get an additional 2.5 billion zloty borrowing limit in the central bank for flood relief purposes but Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz stressed this would not mean pumping extra 2.5 billion zlotys into the economy.
The central bank said earlier on Tuesday it was ready to lend the government up to one billion zlotys for flood relief, but would also collect deposits to offset the monetary effect of such a loan.
The government will also seek an increase in its foreign borrowing limits to accomodate a $300 million loan from the World Bank, he said during a break in a cabinet meeting.
